title: FIFO test and comment LOWs from the WCLI-142 round-2 review (none blocking)
description: Follow-ups from the Opus round-2 APPROVE at e02a1f7 of ward-cli#271 (WCLI-142). L1: the secret-value.ts comment above defaultWait says it is 'not covered by a test', but the FIFO test runs it when a read reports EAGAIN without asserting anything; say it is run by the FIFO test when a read reports EAGAIN, but not asserted. L2: the FIFO test's 500 x 10 ms wait for the writer ties bun's default 5000 ms per-test timeout; shorten the loop or give the test an explicit timeout above the deadline. L3: the FIFO test's finally never kills the writer, so a late writer can block in open(2) and leak; call writer.kill() before awaiting writer.exited, and move Bun.spawn inside the try.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The defaultWait comment states what the FIFO test does and does not assert about it
The FIFO test's wait deadline is shorter than its per-test timeout, or the test sets an explicit timeout above the deadline
A writer that starts late cannot outlive the FIFO test: the test kills it before awaiting its exit, and the spawn is inside the try

implementationNotes: Implemented on fix/WCLI-147-fifo-test-lows, scope exactly L1 to L3, no production behaviour change (only the defaultWait comment in secret-value.ts). L1: the comment now says the real-descriptor FIFO test runs defaultWait when a read reports EAGAIN, but nothing asserts it waited. L2: the writer-opened deadline is 300 x 10 ms (3 s), inside bun's 5 s per-test timeout. Control: a writer that sleeps 6 s before opening the FIFO fails on the test's own assertion (expect(existsSync(opened)).toBe(true), Received false) at 3.5 s, not on a timeout. L3: Bun.spawn moved inside the try and the finally calls writer?.kill() before awaiting its exit; after the late-writer control no writer process was left (pgrep). Pristine test restored after the control; bun run check 1225 pass.

Verdict file 4791 bytes, sha256 bd93a5d8dbe04be07f8656efe6df8d5afe9d7e5f820e0c242c6d6904a73b5430. Merged as squash eb1f99a68633812708f43ce7d279037e88e70546 with Check, Docs and Tracker integrity green on that head. FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE, nothing filed: the one LOW is wording only, 'the deadline is 3 s' in the FIFO test comment is a minimum, not a ceiling.

VERDICT: APPROVE
Review of opum-ai/ward-cli#277 (WCLI-147) at 7f402035f8b91d42791c469b23e71c7c220b9999, read from the tree. Nothing blocks. There is one LOW, which is wording only.

Q1, the L1 comment is TRUE. The comment is at src/adapters/secret-value.ts:111-115. The FIFO test (test/secret.test.ts:1200-1211) passes a `read` port and nothing else. readStdinValueBytes forwards those ports to readOnce (secret-value.ts:254), and readOnce falls back to `ports.wait ?? defaultWait` (:130). The read port calls readSync on an O_NONBLOCK FIFO, so between "first" and "second", and again before the writer closes, readSync throws EAGAIN and defaultWait runs. defaultWait is not exported. No test asserts that it waited. No other test reaches it either: terminal-input.test.ts:37 calls pollInput directly and never goes through readOnce.

Q2, L2 holds. bun's per-test timeout is the 5000 ms default. bunfig.toml sets only `preload`. The preload (test/support/no-real-keychain.ts) has no timeout call. A case-insensitive grep of the repo for setDefaultTimeout and --timeout found nothing, and the `test` script is a bare `bun test`.
The path where the writer never opens: mkfifo spawnSync, then 300 × (existsSync + Bun.sleep(10)), then the assertion at :1198. The finally (closeSync, writeFileSync, kill, await exited) ends fast because SIGTERM interrupts sh whether it is blocked in open(2) or sleeping. The writer measured 3.5 s on this path, about 1.5 s inside 5 s. The margin is lost only if each iteration overshoots its 10 ms by about 6.7 ms or more.
- LOW, test/secret.test.ts:1193-1195. "The deadline is 3 s" overstates the precision. The bound counts iterations, so 3 s is the minimum wall time, not a ceiling. A Date.now() deadline would make the bound exact. As measured, AC index 1 is met.
- Other unbounded waits: none. One pre-existing note, outside L1-L3: readStdinValueBytes is synchronous, so bun's timer cannot preempt the read phase at all. That phase is bounded by the writer's own loop instead: 200 × 0.05 s = 10 s, then EOF at `exec 3>&-`. It can only be reached if the writer opens, writes "first" and then stalls, because the read port writes the marker as soon as its first read returns bytes. This is unchanged since #271.

Q3, L3 holds. Bun.spawn is now inside the try (:1183), with `let writer … | undefined` declared at :1181. The finally calls `writer?.kill()` and then `await writer?.exited` (:1220-1221) on every exit path: success, assertion failure and thrown error.
- If Bun.spawn throws, writer stays undefined, both `?.` calls do nothing, the descriptor is still closed (:1217), and the marker write succeeds because the dir exists. mkfifo and openSync come before the try, and if either fails there is nothing open to leak.
- Killing a writer that already finished: on the success path the read returns 0 only after the writer's final `exec 3>&-`, so kill() reaches a sh that has done all its work and has exited or is exiting. The test never inspects the writer's exit code, so a SIGTERM that lands mid-exit cannot fail it. The success path is what CI runs, so a green run is the runtime proof that kill() does not throw.
- Not a finding: kill() signals only sh's pid, so a `sleep 0.05` child can be orphaned for at most 50 ms. In theory, a throw from closeSync or writeFileSync in the finally would skip the kill. Neither is realistic.

Q4, nothing is weakened. The writer script is byte-identical (diff lines 39 and 50). The three assertions are unchanged: decode equals "firstsecond", at least two reads returned bytes (the offset path), and the opened-marker check. The marker handshake that orders the reads is unchanged. The only behavioural change in the test is 500 → 300 iterations, which reduces start-up slack but weakens no assertion.

Q5, the src change is comment-only: the hunk at secret-value.ts:111-115 touches comment lines and nothing else. No DEC-182 (1) fence-class path is touched: there is no CI, deps or lockfile, settings, hooks, build or auth change. The .quest/tasks/WCLI-147.json diff moves the status to In Progress and adds one implementation note. All three ACs are still unchecked, which fits an open PR.

COULD NOT VERIFY FROM A TREE READ
- CI status at 7f40203, and therefore that kill() on an exited Subprocess does not throw in the Bun version CI resolves.
- That the diff the leader supplied matches the PR's actual file set on GitHub.
- The writer's late-writer control (6 s sleep, 3.5 s failure, pgrep showing no writer left). In particular, I don't know what pgrep matched. If the control was `sleep 6; exec 3>…`, killing sh would orphan the `sleep 6` child, so "no writer left" depends on the pattern used. This does not affect the committed writer, which opens first.
- The "bun run check 1225 pass" figure.
finalSummary: The three FIFO test and comment LOWs from the WCLI-142 round-2 review closed in ward-cli#277 (squash eb1f99a); Opus-model reviewer APPROVE recorded verbatim in the notes. One wording-only LOW (the 3 s deadline is a minimum, not a ceiling) is noted as a follow-up candidate, not filed.
